title: AI-Augmented Service Desk: Ticket Triage, Runbooks, and Knowledge Gap Analysis (2026)

questions.question: Thousands of monthly tickets are fixed from memory while procedures stay unwritten. What precedes any automation?
options: A chatbot over undocumented memory
Trust that analysts never leave
Automating the loudest ticket class first
Auditing each class for knowledge and determinism
questions.explanation: Undocumented memory cannot automate safely. This lesson audits classes into zones before touching automation.

questions.question: How is T-005 classified when the fix is deterministic but no runbook exists?
options: Zone A, because deterministic actions can be automated without documentation
Zone B, because the analyst should see every deterministic fix
Zone D, because an unwritten workaround is always novel
Zone C, because the fix is known but the knowledge signal is absent
questions.explanation: The installation action supplies a determinism signal, but 'No runbook' is excluded by the negation guard and no knowledge signal remains. That combination is Zone.C: document first.

questions.question: What zone does T-003 receive when a SharePoint wiki article exists but the resolution depends on the migrated groups and tenant?
options: Zone B, because knowledge is present while the resolution path remains ambiguous
Zone A, because any wiki article makes the ticket deterministic
Zone C, because all SharePoint tickets lack a standard fix
Zone D, because a partial article is counted as no knowledge
questions.explanation: The wiki article gives one knowledge signal, while the resolution text has no deterministic signal. classify_ticket maps knowledge-high and determinism-low to Zone.B analyst augmentation.

questions.question: Which zone does T-006 receive when neither a documented procedure nor a deterministic fix is described?
options: Zone A, because the classifier assumes common 500 errors are standard
Zone D, because the ticket is novel or complex on both dimensions
Zone C, because every unknown fix is documentation work
Zone B, because an analyst can resolve every ambiguous ticket from the surface
questions.explanation: T-006 has no affirmative knowledge signal and lists several possible causes rather than a deterministic resolution. Both signal classes are low, so the classifier returns Zone.D.

questions.question: What automation verdict does score_runbook return for AD Account Unlock (AD-04)?
options: SURFACE, because machine_readability is only 1
DOCUMENT, because every runbook needs YAML before automation
READY, because its total is 9/10 and it qualifies for Zone A shadow mode
ESCALATE, because account operations cannot be automated
questions.explanation: The dimensions sum to 2+2+2+1+2 = 9. score_runbook marks totals of at least 7 READY and notes that shadow mode should precede state-changing automation.

questions.question: What verdict does score_runbook give VPN Reconnect macOS (NET-11) with a total of 4/10?
options: READY, because the runbook has a named owner
DOCUMENT, because scores from 4 through 6 are too low for any analyst surface
ESCALATE, because a PDF runbook is always a safety incident
SURFACE, because 4/10 falls in the analyst-augmentation range
questions.explanation: The scorer maps totals 4–6 to AutomationVerdict.SURFACE. The PDF's zero machine-readability dimension is reported, but the runbook remains useful to an analyst while it is improved.
